Know what is available, what remains under validation, and what a website account or saved cart actually means. What is P.O.P.S.? P.O.P.S. means Proof of Presence System. It is installable Windows software designed primarily for fathers documenting parenting-time experiences. Its purpose is to bring event notes, supporting files, case context, and chronology together for personal review and discussions with counsel. The website is the product and customer-access surface; it is not your private Evidence Vault. Is there a mandatory subscription? The standard Windows license follows a one-time purchase model without a mandatory recurring subscription. The existing published Guardian price is $99. Optional annual maintenance is listed at $19.99, but its precise coverage and launch availability require confirmation. No new recurring plan, automatic renewal, or lifetime upgrade entitlement is promised here. Checkout is currently unavailable. What does Guardian Access include? The published offer describes a Windows desktop license with lifetime P.O.P.S. Membership included. Feature availability depends on the release supplied. Supported Windows versions, device limits, update rights, installation requirements, delivery timing, and refund terms must be finalized before purchases open. Android access is not promised as part of this license. How is beta participation different from buying? Beta enrollment expresses interest in testing and providing feedback. A saved application is not an invitation, a paid license, or a guaranteed place. The program aims for 50 active participants. Participation terms and any access arrangements will be supplied with an invitation. Purchasing does not automatically enroll you in testing. What is the first-100 customer program? The founding-customer presentation is intended for the first 100 qualifying paying customers. Special benefits and qualification rules are not yet approved. There is no discount or additional entitlement to claim today. A cart item or account registration does not establish first-100 status; that would require verified qualifying completed purchases. Is Android available? POPS Android is progressing through Google Play testing. It is not publicly available, approved for production, or ready to purchase. There is no public Play Store listing or Android price. A Windows Guardian license, Open Door assistance, or sponsor-funded Windows access does not grant Android access. See the Android page for testing status and planned workflows. Does a hash prove that an event happened? No. SHA-256 can help compare file contents with a recorded reference. It does not establish that an event occurred, that a statement is accurate, or that a location or timestamp is independently verified. Provenance and handling context are separate records. Users remain responsible for accuracy and lawful collection. Can I export an attorney-ready packet? Structured timelines, selected files, indexes, manifests, and integrity reports are intended handoff outputs. Exact formats and contents require verification against the release being supplied. Do not assume every listed output is available. Counsel decides what is useful for a matter; P.O.P.S. does not guarantee legal acceptance or admissibility. Privacy Principle POPS is designed around a local-first principle: family records should remain under the user's control unless the user deliberately chooses to export, share, upload, submit, or transmit them. The POPS website and the POPS desktop application serve different functions. The website is a public information, support, and access channel. The desktop application is intended to help users organize their own case records locally. POPS does not promise automatic cloud backup, encrypted storage, attorney sharing, permanent evidence preservation, or remote access unless a specific active product feature clearly states that it is enabled and explains how it works. 2. This may include information such as browser type, device type, IP address, page request information, timestamps, and referral source. POPS does not use this information to build profiles about a user's private family case, child, court matter, medical situation, or legal dispute. 3. Information POPS Does Not Request Through General Forms Do not send private case evidence through a general POPS contact form, social-media message, ordinary support email, Open Door request, or Noted Counsel submission. It is informational and is not a referral marketplace. No Rank. No Referral. Only Merit. POPS Noted Counsel is a positive-only merit-recognition page for attorneys who made a meaningful positive impression on a POPS user. Recognition may reflect professionalism, honesty, preparation, respectful treatment, clear communication, or meaningful service to a parent trying to stay present and organized for their child. What This Is POPS Noted Counsel exists to preserve and share carefully moderated positive recognition from real POPS users who had a direct, first-hand experience with an attorney. It is meant to recognize merit—not popularity, advertising budget, status, or influence. What This Is Not Not an attorney ranking system Not a star-rating or score-based review page Not a paid attorney directory Not a referral service or lead-generation program Not a “best attorney” list Not a public complaint board Not a guarantee that an attorney will accept a case or achieve a result Recognition Rules Only POPS Noted Users may submit a Merit Recognition. A Noted Counsel recognition does not claim that an attorney is superior to another attorney. It does not promise a legal result, availability, affordability, or case acceptance. Why POPS Built This POPS helps fathers and parents arrive more prepared—with clearer timelines, preserved records, factual notes, and organized materials for professional review. This walkthrough follows Alex, a fictional father documenting an exchange that did not take place. The example explains the intended workflow without claiming that a demonstration is a real case or proof of an event. Release clarity Steps describe the product workflow. Exact screens, supported file types, integrity checks, and export functions depend on the tested release. Actual release captures will be added after verification. 1. Capture what you personally observed Alex starts with the scheduled exchange date, the agreed place, and a short factual note about what happened. A useful entry separates the planned event from the observed result. It avoids guessing about another person's motives or turning a disagreement into a legal conclusion. The benefit is context while the details are fresh. Instead of returning weeks later to reconstruct a confusing afternoon, Alex has an identifiable event to review. If a detail is uncertain, the note should say so rather than invent precision. Use fictional records while learning the software. The website beta form is for contact and platform information, not for submitting the exchange details or the supporting evidence. 2. Keep supporting material and its source context Alex associates a harmless example message and receipt with the event. Source notes explain where each item came from and whether it is an original export, screenshot, or other copy. A screenshot can be useful without being equivalent to the underlying source record. Where supported by the release, file hashing creates a reference fingerprint for later comparison. It can help identify a change in file contents. It does not establish that Alex was at a location or that the account of the exchange is true. Original-file preservation, metadata retention, and custody logging must be verified before relying on a specific build. Keep independent source material and appropriate backups. 3. Connect the pieces in a chronology Alex connects the event with its supporting files and relevant order reference. The timeline gives the event a place among other dated records. That makes it easier to find the right material when preparing for a discussion. Organization is useful even when a record is incomplete. A missing attachment or uncertain date should remain visible as a gap. The software should not be presented as filling gaps with independently verified facts. The Windows workspace is the primary product. Mobile capture and Windows–Android synchronization are forthcoming work; this example does not depend on an announced synchronization feature. 4. Review the record before interpreting it Alex reads the event in sequence, checks the attached material, and corrects any inaccurate notes. Dates, source labels, names, and the distinction between observation and inference all matter. A repeated sequence can prompt a question without establishing a legal finding. The practical benefit is a clearer starting point for review. A lawyer can ask about a specific event and its source context instead of receiving an unexplained collection of images. Protect. Prove. The Creed The Charge I am the First Order of Protection. Before the law arrives, I am here. Before the danger is named, I am watching. Before my family asks, I have already decided: I will not fail them. I do not wait for permission to protect what is mine. I do not require a title to fulfill a calling. My badge is my presence. My oath was sworn the day I accepted this house as my charge. I will preserve what has been entrusted to me. I will protect those who cannot yet protect themselves. I will prove, by action, not by word, that the watchman did not sleep. Preserve Protect Prove This is not a slogan. This is the order of operations for every day I am given breath. The Pledge of Commitment I make this pledge not to an institution, but to the ones under my roof, and before the God who placed them in my care. Presence I pledge my presence: that I will be found, that I will be reachable, that I will not be a stranger in my own home. Vigilance I pledge my vigilance: that I will see the danger before it announces itself, and act before I am asked. Readiness I pledge my readiness: that whatever the moment requires, I will not be found unprepared, untrained, or unwilling. Record I pledge my record: that my actions will speak, and that if ever questioned, the proof of what I did and when I did it will stand on its own. Restraint I pledge my restraint: that my strength exists to shield, not to dominate; my authority exists to serve, not to rule. Permanence I pledge my permanence: that this charge does not end at the end of a shift, a season, or a hard year. It ends when I do, and not before. This is the First Order. It is a support machine. It was built for the father who is being denied access to his child and needs to move through the system with discipline, proof, and restraint. Not panic. Not revenge. Not desperation. A record. POPS exists because when a father's presence is questioned, emotion is not enough. Memory is not enough. Pain is not enough. The record has to stand. The Mission There is a place in a father that does not need to be taught. The instinct to protect. The duty to stand between harm and the child. The responsibility to show up, provide, guard, and remain accountable even when nobody is watching. That duty is not created by a court order. It is older than that. It lives in conscience, in blood, in faith, and in the charge placed inside a man to protect what has been entrusted to him. So when a father is separated from his child, that calling does not disappear. It becomes trapped. He is still a protector, but the door is locked. He is still responsible, but his hands are tied. He is still called a father, but treated like a visitor. He still carries the duty, but is denied the place to perform it. POPS was built for that place. Not to attack. Not to inflame. Not to spy. Presence is the call made, the message sent, the arrival at the exchange, the request for records, the follow-up after silence, and the lawful attempt when the door does not open. POPS is designed to help preserve a record of those attempts for later review. Protection Protection means guarding the child, the truth, the record, and the lawful path forward. Not aggression. Declaration First Order of Protection and Service Mission Statement POPS - the Proof of Presence System - exists to restore men to their God-given appointment as the First Order of Protection in the home. It equips fathers with the discipline, record-keeping, and truth-preserving tools needed to stand watch over their families, remain accountable in conflict, and protect what has been entrusted to them. POPS strengthens the man, safeguards the record, and preserves the truth when presence is questioned, challenged, or denied. POPS is not a support group. It is a support machine - built to keep a man aligned, sober-minded, and anchored to his calling, even in the hardest seasons of fatherhood. About This Declaration The P.O.P.S. Declaration is the foundational document of the First Order of Protection. It is not a policy, a slogan, or a motivational speech. It is the formal articulation of what men have always been in the home: the first responder, the first defender, the first witness, and the first line of protection long before institutions existed. This Declaration defines the charge, the duty, and the office of the father - not as a cultural role, but as a God-given appointment. It affirms the rights, responsibilities, and presence of the man who stands between his family and the dark, and calls that role by its true name: P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System. Preamble When in the course of a family's life, danger does not announce itself, when the call for help cannot wait for sirens, when the wolf is at the door and the door is the only thing between the wolf and the children, there must stand, in that gap, a man. Not a badge. Not a uniform. A father. Before there were Courts of Protection Services, before there were County Officers of Public Safety, before any institution wore the name of guardian, there was the man of the house, standing watch, armed with nothing but resolve and the authority given to him by his Creator. We call this what it has always been: P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System. The First Order of Protection and Service. This is not a replacement for law. This is the foundation law was built upon. When the C.O.P.S. cannot get there in time, and there will be moments they cannot, the P.O.P.S. is already there. He was never not there. That is the whole of the charge. We hold these truths to be self-evident, God-given, and undeniable: that every father is entrusted with rights, privileges, and responsibilities that no government granted and no government may revoke; that presence is not passive but is itself a duty; and that a man who stands watch over his household stands in an office older than nations. Purpose and Operating Doctrine P.O.P.S. - Proof of Presence System - helps parents organize facts, preserve records, document good-faith effort, and prepare clearer materials for attorney or court review. POPS is not a law firm. POPS does not provide legal advice, legal representation, legal strategy, or a guarantee of any court result, attorney acceptance, evidence admissibility, or case outcome. 1.1 Core Principle Turn emotion into facts. Turn facts into organized proof. Turn proof into a clearer case file. 1.2 Product Boundary POPS is built to help a parent document what happened, identify the supporting record, organize chronology, and prepare materials for review. It is not built to attack another parent, create revenge material, spy on anyone, or tell a user what legal action to take. 2. Acceptable Use Policy Users must use POPS lawfully, honestly, and with respect for the privacy and rights of others. 2.1 Prohibited Uses Creating, altering, fabricating, or misrepresenting evidence Using POPS to stalk, intimidate, threaten, harass, or retaliate Accessing another person's device, account, or private records without permission Uploading or sharing private information through unapproved channels Using POPS as a substitute for emergency services or qualified legal counsel Presenting POPS-generated material as legal advice, a court order, or verified fact without review 3.
